People in India are switching to UPI because paying now takes a few seconds and a phone, with no cash, no card and no waiting. Launched in 2016, it links straight to your bank account, so money moves between accounts instantly, any day and any hour, even on holidays.

Three reasons stand out:

It's quick and simple. Scan a QR code or type a mobile number, enter your PIN, done. There are no account numbers or bank details to copy.
It's free for most people. Sending money to friends and paying small shops usually costs nothing, while cards and wallets often carry fees.
It works everywhere. From big shops to chai stalls and vegetable carts, a printed QR code is all a seller needs. No card machine is required.

Trust matters too. Your PIN protects every payment, and you get an instant message for each one. Many people also like that one app can pay bills, split costs with friends and send money across different banks. Once the sellers in your neighbourhood accept it, going back to cash feels slow.
